editorial:
Imagine being told you have to marry a complete stranger just to help your dad's business. That is exactly the mess Rosemary finds herself in. To get away from the pressure, she heads back to Europe, but she is not the only one running. She meets Peter, a guy who is also trying to avoid his own family obligations. The funny part is that they both use fake names, so they fall in love without even knowing they are actually the two people forced to marry each other. It feels like a lighthearted game of hide-and-seek with romance mixed in, making the whole vibe feel breezy and sweet.

You will really enjoy the chemistry between the leads and the silly misunderstandings that keep the plot moving. While the pacing is a bit slower than modern rom-coms, the charm of the 1960s setting makes up for it. If you love old-school romance with a twist, you should definitely track this one down.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the truth about their real names finally comes out. After spending the movie lying to each other, they realize they were actually the intended business partners all along. Instead of being angry, they are thrilled because they already love each other for who they really are. They tell their fathers that they will marry, but on their own terms, ending the movie with a happy and romantic reunion.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic romantic comedies and stories about fate.
